title: What Does It Mean To Be Made In The Image Of God
paragraphs: Understanding the Doctrine: Made in the Image of God

The concept of being made in the image of God, known in Latin as imago Dei, is one of the foundational truths of Scripture regarding humanity. This profound truth shapes our understanding of human dignity, purpose, and destiny. But what does it truly mean to be made in God's image?
The Biblical Foundation
The Bible first introduces this concept in the opening chapter of Genesis:

And God said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the birds of the heavens, and over the cattle, and over all the earth, and over every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth. And God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them. - Genesis 1:26-27 ASV
Here, Scripture affirms that both male and female are made in God's image, setting humanity apart from the rest of creation. But what does this entail?
What the Image of God Is Not

The image of God does not mean that humans physically resemble God, as God is spirit (John 4:24 ASV). Nor does it mean that humans are divine or possess God's attributes in their fullness. Instead, the image is about reflecting certain aspects of God's character and function.
Key Aspects of the Image of God
Relational Capacity:
Humans, unlike animals, have a unique capacity for relationship—with God and with one another. We are created for fellowship, reflecting the relational nature of the Triune God (Genesis 2:18 ASV).
Moral and Spiritual Nature:
Humanity is endowed with a moral conscience and the ability to discern right from wrong. Paul affirms this moral sense in all people (Romans 2:14-15 ASV).
Creativity and Stewardship:
Just as God is Creator, humans have been given the ability to create, cultivate, and exercise dominion over the earth (see Genesis 1:28 ASV). We are called to steward God's creation responsibly.
Rationality and Intellect:
Humans can think, reason, and plan, reflecting God's wisdom. This capacity for knowledge and understanding is distinct in humanity (Proverbs 2:6 ASV).
Capacity for Worship:
Above all, humans are created to know, love, and worship God. This is our highest calling and fulfillment (Psalm 95:6 ASV).
The Image of God After the Fall
Though humanity fell into sin, the image of God was not destroyed, but marred. After the Fall, God still affirms the value of human life based on this image:
Whoso sheddeth man's blood, by man shall his blood be shed: For in the image of God made he man. - Genesis 9:6 ASV
James also reminds us that all people, regardless of their spiritual state, bear God's image and are therefore worthy of respect:
Therewith bless we the Lord and Father; and therewith curse we men, who are made after the likeness of God. - James 3:9 ASV
The Image Restored in Christ
God's ultimate purpose is to restore His image in us through Jesus Christ. Through salvation and sanctification, believers are being renewed after the likeness of Christ:
and have put on the new man, that is being renewed unto knowledge after the image of him that created him. - Colossians 3:10 ASV
For whom he foreknew, he also foreordained to be conformed to the image of his Son... - Romans 8:29 ASV
Ultimately, the full restoration of the image of God will come in glory, when believers are made like Christ (1 John 3:2 ASV).
Practical Implications
Human Dignity: Every person has inherent worth and value, regardless of age, ability, ethnicity, or status.
Sanctity of Life: The image of God is the basis for the protection of all human life.
Purpose and Mission: We are called to reflect God's character, steward creation, and point others to Christ.
Conclusion

To be made in the image of God is to be created for relationship, reflection, and representation. Though marred by sin, this image is being restored in all who trust in Christ. Our identity and mission are rooted in this profound truth.
Related Questions You Might Ask
